I have found this to help when performing a VLOOKUP - instead of going through and cleaning up the data after the fact, you can perform a clean VLOOKUP this way:

=IFERROR(TRIM(VLOOKUP(A2,H1:H99,1,FALSE)),"")

H1:H99 = Range --> I also find it easier to name the range first and reference it using the name when typing out the function.

I have to say, Charter has come a long way. I've had them for years as my ISP. Probably about 5 or more years ago they hit rock bottom, then they began to turn things around in a major way and started with their customer service. Shortly after they got that to a decent level, they focused on speeds. They got rid of their data cap (which wasn't really enforced, but was still in the terms) and increased the speeds without increasing their rates.

Now, they still do promotional rates, so you still have to call them every 6-12 months to get into a new promotion, but every time I call, I usually don't have to say anything, the rep just says, "Oh it looks like you're paying a regular rate, let's see what kind of promotion we can get you back into." I called them recently to look into adding TV service for the first time in a long while and there weren't any high pressure sales techniques to get me into a higher package or anything like that. She was honestly trying to help me get the channels I wanted for the best price.
